quote.text: I have no idea where my money went

promise.text: How to import a bank statement CSV: check the file first

art.why: the carousel's topic: the moment and its guide name "statement", "csv"

lines.text: Download the file, check its shape, map the columns and catch duplicate rows, plus what a list of past transactions cannot tell you.

eyebrow.text: Import a file in six steps

body.text: Name each file with its last date, like bank-2026-09-30.csv.
We'd take a month at a time, because each file then starts where the last one ended and no days overlap.

eyebrow.text: Import a file in six steps

head.text: Open a copy in a text editor, not a spreadsheet.

body.text: Look for the header row, the date order and any amount with a comma or a bracket around it.

eyebrow.text: Import a file in six steps

body.text: Either one Amount column where spending is negative, or a Debit column and a Credit column with positive numbers in each.
If your bank shows spending as positive, note it before you map.

eyebrow.text: Import a file in six steps

head.text: Map the columns: date, description and amount, or date, description, debit and credit.

body.text: Leave out any running balance column.

eyebrow.text: Import a file in six steps

body.text: Check for repeated rows, transfers between your own accounts and refunds.

line.text: Transactions you enter or import, reviewed before anything joins your picture, so what you are looking at is what actually happened.
